statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WASHINGTON, D.C., IS A MATH-FREE ZONE
statements.title: WASHINGTON, D.C., IS A MATH-FREE ZONE
sentences: Every workday, the Joint Economic Committee sends out a text message and it is basically what we call the daily debt.
The total debt is--and I think this chart is from yesterday--$40.662 trillion.
We also try to add in here when we hit the debt ceiling.
Right now our prediction is February 22, we hit the U.S. debt ceiling, which I think is $41 trillion and a couple hundred billion on top of that.
I spent 16 years of my life here basically doing the same damn thing, trying to get this place to be willing to understand the debt, deficit, and demographics.
The majority of our debt is driven by our demographics, but we are not allowed to talk about that.
The way we approach the solutions does break down, and I am going to show you a whole bunch of ``tax the rich,'' but the math doesn't come close to reality.

Mr. Speaker, if anyone out there really wants to understand what is going on and see it on a daily basis and know it down to the second of borrowing, Joint Economic Committee Republicans, you can sign up for the daily debt.
It is things like Medicare, Social Security, Medicaid, other mandatory spending.
We are down to only 24 percent of the Federal spending we vote on now, and it is what we call nondefense discretionary and defense.
Number one spend is Social Security.
When someone says they stole my Social Security.
Medicaid and ObamaCare subsidies, we need to talk about that because if I get one more person who goes and says they cut it.
These other things-- Social Security, interest, Medicare, Medicaid, and ObamaCare subsidies--your government is an insurance company with an Army.
I can get rid of every dime of defense--defense spending in 2026 is $965 billion.
The different colors are different types of taxes: personal income tax, corporate taxes, and it is part of the fraud here.
It is not like Europe or other countries where a substantial portion of their taxes is basically a consumption tax.
Then you get this asinine: Well, we will just tax the rich.
I know it is almost unreadable from a distance, but it is basically: How do you end up in a debt crisis cycle?
How about the entire country is, functionally, living on an edge because if the United States hits a debt wall, we functionally bring down the rest of the world's economy.
We are actually well into this debt cycle where we are having to issue more Treasury bonds because interest rates are up.
Because interest rates are up, the cost of the debt is more.
It is like the problem on the ACA, the ObamaCare.
We are going to subsidize more of this, then we are going to borrow the money that we are giving out as a subsidy, so interest rates go up more, the debt goes up more.
Remember, I just showed you the debt cycle chart.
It is because we are terrified to actually redesign the programs that are bingeing on debt.

I am a big, big fan of adopting technology all up and down the Federal Government to basically have as efficient a workforce, maybe as small a workforce as possible, but even here we basically have gone from 3 million Federal employees to 2.7 million, yet the cost and the debt of that has still just gone up fairly dramatically.
Do you remember the hacking away at Medicaid?
Okay, this one is the TANF chart, 1997 basically through 2025, so a full year.

The one that will drive you a little nuts--and the chart actually has a weird blip because during some of COVID we actually used different accounts to fund parts of Medicaid--Medicaid spending last year was up over 8 percent.
Mr. Speaker, how many times did you have an opponent or have you heard Democrats or commentators on television saying: ``They cut Medicaid''?
Okay, once again, what is Medicaid?
Medicaid was a deal put together, substantially, in the 1960s, the Federal Government would cover half the burden if the State covered the other half of the burden, and it was for indigents.
Turn all of Medicaid spending, saying we are going to send you the dollars, State, you don't get to draw down more dollars.
I didn't bring the chart, but if anyone actually wants to double-check what I am saying, New York City, the number one job creator over the last 5 years is a Medicaid home visiting program.
All the tax proposals--and these things are really regressive because these things would not be just tax the rich.
Let's go on and let's actually take a look here and see if I can find the chart that showed actually: Okay, what if we said let's just tax the rich.
Let's do the wealth tax, okay?
We are going to take the wealthy, the really wealthy in America, and we are going to basically do a surtax on them.
Okay, big chart here, this is the Medicare for All, over 10.7 percent of the entire economy.
So this is their ``tax the rich'' proposals: once again, universal healthcare, reparations, and Federal job guarantees.

This is the classic problem: When we basically see a wealth tax, and I believe that is based on the math from the Elizabeth Warren wealth tax, you will notice it is not even maybe point three-quarters of a percent.
How about an 8 percent wealth tax?
And it says: Hey, an 8 percent wealth tax.

If we start to look at the bond markets around the world, the debt markets around the world, functionally, no, I am not supposed to curse, and my 4-year-old is sitting behind me, but we lie our heinies off.
Think of the things going on in France right now, the protests, the fights over what the retirement age should be, these things.
And we are the reserve currency, at least right now we are, for the world.
For us, often when we are home, we will get folks who turn to us and say: David, I don't like it when foreigners buy our debt.
Foreign central banks are buying a lot less of our debt.
So we buy stuff from them, we send them our money, and we don't want them buying our sovereign debt.

The fact of the matter is when a Japanese central bank or German central bank buys and holds U.S. sovereign debt, it is partially to stabilize their own currency, that is the currency of trade, and they don't sell and trade it.
Trading houses are buying our debt.
If you take a look at some of the charts over the last couple of years, has anyone been paying attention to how erratic U.S. sovereign debt instruments are?
We are subject to a market that is becoming much more erratic because those who are buying our debt now are much less other central banks because we also are selling so damn much debt.
This is how we ultimately walk back into a debt crisis.
However, when we start seeing political people like in France right now: Let's just take a certain amount of our debt and not pay it.
That debt isn't sitting in some banker's bank account.
Mr. Speaker, the next time you get someone who tells you: We are going to grow our way out of the debt.
At current interest rates, debt to GDP grows to 162 percent in 9 budget years, and that is publicly borrowed debt.

We see numbers here that basically say that starting in 2035 the percentage of debt to GDP, the percentage of interest consuming the available tax collections--remember, we don't get to spend on this, this spike of taxes, Social Security taxes, Medicare taxes, the unemployment tax, the disability tax.
In 2032, the Social Security trust fund will be empty.

Those of you who want more people on social programs, more infrastructure, and would like to fix airports, you are only a few years away from half of all of our inbound tax receipts that are available, other than Social Security and Medicare, going to just interest.

Mr. Speaker, as my experience here has been, I have introduced legislation that would result in the biggest spending cuts in U.S. history, and no one would get a cut in their services because it was going to redesign some of the ways we deliver things in Medicare.
I am going to show a couple charts here that show times when we have had very high marginal tax rates, very low marginal tax rates, and you are going to see a consistency.
They call it a VAT tax, and I am going to show you the spending is so out of control.
Even when you do a value-added tax, it doesn't come close to covering all the new proposals that we are going to be getting from this new Democratic Congress.
As interest rates go up--my last couple of boards I am going to show you is back to that concept of interest fragility.
I am going to show you that in about 9 years, almost half of the available taxes in the United States Federal Government will go to interest.
Now, maybe we will never get the budgets right.
We will just pretend we can keep borrowing until, functionally, the bond market says no.
I am going to show you some of the fragility in that in a couple boards from now.
I am going to show this chart.

If you would like to have something less than a 6.5 percent mortgage right now, get this Federal Government to convince the bond markets that we are going to actually start being responsible and borrowing less money.
I am going to keep moving until we find that chart.
This was discourse in this last election of: We are going to tax rich people, and we are going to get all this new free stuff.
How many days before the bond market basically says: Screw you, we are going to raise your interest rate?
I will show you some charts at the end here of just how dangerous these numbers are.
What happens when we tell you: Hey, we are going to grow at 3 percent of GDP.
In 2035, we will technically hit the mathematical crisis zone that has set off other economies into free fall.
Grandma will get a 22- to 24-percent cut in her check, and we will double senior poverty.
I will help you cut the spending so it works.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MATH PROBLEM
statements.title: MATH PROBLEM
sentences: Unlike our friends on the left, I am going to actually show you the math and the facts that taxing the rich can't get you anywhere close, anywhere close to the actual receipts required to make a difference.
The primary driver of U.S. debt is almost the thing we as elected officials aren't allowed to talk about.
In about 20 something months, the majority of Federal spending will go to those of us over 65.

What have we done to our kids when we need every dime a child functioning under 5 years old today, every dime they will ever make in their lifetime, is required to cover Social Security, Medicare, military retirement, the healthcare side, and the pension side--just the pensions of the Federal Government?
It is about the adoption of technology.
It is the holistic circle of everything from tele-based immigration, to the adoption of technology, to redesigning, to cures, to taking on obesity.
Maybe the cures and doing things that are moral are the most powerful things we can do for the debt, deficit, and spending.
When we borrow from the Social Security trust fund and the Medicare trust fund, we pay it back interest.
Yet, the debt and deficit continues to explode.

If we raise the individual income tax, if we raise capital gains tax, if we do all of these things, we even tax their retirement accounts, and then we effect--do it where the maximum tax rate before it rolls over economically, because when you--you can raise a tax--concept: You have a job.
The punch line is when you do the economic effects, you get 1.1 to 2 percent of the economy in new taxes.

I am going to show you a couple of boards here where to even cover the trillions of dollars of additional spending the Democrats have promised, you can't get close to financing it from billionaires or even multimillionaires.
At the same time, the debt is still going to go up.
Last year, 31 percent--remember, you cannot spend the FICA tax, the payroll tax, the tax that goes to Social Security, Medicare, unemployment, disability.
If interest rates move up a bit, it could be over half of all the tax receipts that are available don't go to roads, cures, welfare benefits, or whatever you desire.
The single biggest things Republicans and Democrats need to do is tell the truth about the country's demographics and the debt and what we call interest fragility.
Proposed tax increases--if you look at these two charts side by side, you are going to actually see adding another 10 percent on payroll caps, and also no cap on Social Security taxes.
If any of you have ever done an advanced economics class, you have had this discussion of debt fragility, of how you end up in a world where you borrow and have to refinance more.
You have to do more, and then you have to issue more debt.
That gap is the debt and deficits.
That excess pool of savings is what has financed the governments all over the world to binge on debt.
If I get another idiot who says: ``Well, what about the data centers?'' Understand, the entire borrowing in data centers is a fraction of what the United States is going to borrow this year.

The point you and I are making: This many savers, this much excess savings in the world, this much borrowing from governments and data centers and anyone else buying a house or borrowing or buying a car, when you are borrowing that money, what you are doing is you are borrowing the money from excess savers.
It is beyond the fact that there is a data center somewhere out there borrowing money.

If you understand that you have $40 trillion--actually, $40.5 trillion--we are going to hit the debt ceiling in this country in the first week or two of March, and that means every 145, 148 days, we are clicking off another $1 trillion in borrowing.

Some of it is incredibly moral because we fixate on our brothers and sisters being helped there: The adoption of technology all through government, the ability that we can build more houses, do these things by adopting technology.
Congressional Budget Office last February said in nine budget years, 2036, the U.S. debt will be $3.1 trillion, $2.1 trillion of that being interest, $1 trillion being the structural.

The fact of the matter is, when central banks around the world bought U.S. debt, they bought it because we were trading in U.S. dollars, and it created a level of stability because they didn't care if interest rates were up or down, they just held that debt, and it created a band on U.S. sovereign interest rates.
As more and more of your debt is held by traders, the trading house's job is to make marginal dollars off the movements of the values of those bonds.
It is not to just hold it as an offset to the value of their currency.
Yet, I will still see people get up in front of audiences: We don't want foreigners buying our debt.
If they are willing to turn around and buy our debt and create low interest rate stability, bless their precious hearts.
That is the capital gains tax, which is half.
At current interest rates, debt-to- GDP growth--now, I need you to hear what I am saying.
In 9 years, 2036, with these current interest rates, we are at 162 percent of debt to GDP as an economy.
If you are a European economist, you don't play the game the United States says as, well, that is publicly sold debt.
We have economists now that are saying: David, you start to hit the crisis zone--this is using the traditional debt-to-GDP ratio.
In 6, 7 years from now, from a traditional debt-to-GDP model, you are hitting the crisis zone.
Our fragility is when you start to hit those zones, do the bond markets, the debt markets start to say: We want a premium on U.S. sovereign debt?
You already saw there are 13 other industrialized countries that can sell their 10-year debt cheaper than we can.
Once again, we, in the general fund, do not get to spend your FICA tax, your Social Security, your Medicare, your unemployment, or your disability.
We are going to issue another $2 trillion in virgin debt so there is the multiplier effect.
We did the laddering of the old debt that we had from a few years ago in which the very low interest rates get rolled into these higher interest rates.

Tell them that the majority of the income taxes, the corporate taxes, the capital gains taxes, the excise taxes, all those, that the majority of it in 9 years is going to go just to pay the financing costs of previous years' spending.
I am going to show you the math.
People say, ``David, I know you are right, but that business is based in my district, and I can't vote for the reforms.'' Screw them.
My 4-year-old son, we will need 104 percent of his lifetime earnings just to pay Federal Government pensions.
These idiots who sometimes say: David, we are going to grow our way out.
OMB said, hey, we are going to take in $6 trillion in '26.
CBO, we are going to take in $5.6 trillion.
And for all of you who somehow are a part of the, well, if we just raise taxes, I am going to show you a couple of charts here.
On the next couple of boards I am going to show you, we get about 17 to 18 percent of GDP.
I have had a stunning amount of coffee already today, so I am going to try and stop yelling at the microphone.
It basically said: Let's take everything the Democrats have been saying, from Bernie Sanders to Elizabeth Warren, here are all the tax hikes we are going to do on rich people.
Do we poll test how we are going to take on math?
At the same time, we are going to drive interest rates higher.

At the same time--I am going to show you some boards in a couple of minutes where we did the modeling with CBO, and, hopefully, I can say this three times in the speech so maybe someone will hear it--we are making a prediction that in 9 budget years, almost half the available taxes will be interest.
In 2036, 9 years, 9 budget years from now, I am going to show you a chart where interest rates as they are today, it is about 44 percent of all tax receipts.
We will put these all up on the Republican side of the Joint Economic Committee.
We are going to redo this, but our current model says in nine budget years, the structural deficit is over $3.8 trillion.
My fear is I am going to use at least 10 of it, and I apologize to my friend from Texas.
Sorry, one of these days--I hopefully will never, never put you through it--I will do a whole presentation on different tax structures and where you maximize economic growth and minimize taxes.
But I am going to ask you to think beyond that.
On this last board, I am going to ask you to try to hear me.

The craziness of the left saying we are going to spend another $5 trillion on top of everything else, plus another $2 trillion on top of that in finance costs and we are going to finance it with rich people is an absolute lie.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REALITY OF THE MATH
statements.title: REALITY OF THE MATH
sentences: Think of this: In the last 5 years, U.S. debt has gone up by one- third.
Mr. Speaker, think about this: This coming January, we are going to hit the debt ceiling again.
It was only a couple of years ago that we actually raised the debt ceiling by $5 trillion, and we have already almost burned through it.

When you start to look over here, Medicare, Social Security, Medicaid, other things that are in the formulas, and interest, I need everyone to understand something: Social Security is the number one spend in our government and probably will come in about $1.6 trillion.
Medicaid will come in at about $1 trillion, Medicaid and ObamaCare subsidies.
That is where you borrow money from the trust fund, Social Security, Medicare, which those trust funds are gone, functionally, in 6 years.

Cascade events start to shoot up those interest rates, and when you are carrying a total of $40 trillion in debt, $32 trillion to $33 trillion of that we have sold, $10 trillion of it we have to refinance every year, do you understand the danger you have put this country in?

An increase in dependency on the market-based--the reason I am showing you this chart is one of the things that is happening around the world and been happening to U.S. debt for the last couple of years is a lot of the Federal Reserve banks of different countries have been sort of holding their amount of U.S. debt steady as we are still borrowing more money, meaning more and more of our debt is being purchased by bond houses, trading houses.
The debt is being purchased by those who trade it, pledge it, buy options on it, sell it.
When the central Bank of Japan or Germany or someone else buys U.S. debt, they are holding it basically as an offset to their own currency, and it is stable.
A whole portion of our debt today is in play, so those of you who used to say: I don't want other countries buying our debt--I can show you chart after chart.
If they are willing to buy our debt, it pushes down our interest rates, and if it is their central banks buying it, it actually makes our debt more stable.
I believe we are like 13 or 14 in the debt stack of industrialized countries.
Meaning, the market has decided they are more creditworthy than the United States even though we are the reserve currency of the world.
In the bond market we call it a term premium on U.S. debt.

If you actually look at the compounding piling of new debt being sold--remember, in the United States this year--and we have a fairly decent economy--for every dollar we are taking in in tax collection, we are spending $1.40.
A few years ago I did a presentation on the debt and deficit and demographics.
Remember, the primary driver of our debt is our demographics.
If you can't convince the debt markets that we are creditworthy, that we belong having lower interest rates--all this has to be refinanced, and we are refinancing it now at higher interest rates.
That means over 7 percent mortgage rates on a 30-year debt.
All I am trying to show you there is that most of the future financing is driven by interest, not the actual debt.
But back then in February, the number was, in 2036, 9 budget years from now, you will have a $3.1 trillion debt.
What happens in a world where the primary driver of your debt is actually paying the interest on previous spending?
The primary driver of U.S. debt and the debt from the entire industrialized world is our demographics.
Maybe the entire world is tired of giving those who are bingeing on debt a free ride.
If you actually look at current interest rates, debt to GDP grows to 162 percent in 10 years.
If you do total debt-- remember, this is total debt--so you are over 100 percent of debt to GDP.
Right now, we are close to $33 trillion in publicly sold debt.
The rest of the world actually calculates their debt that way.
When you hear us say, well, we are only at 101 or 102 percent of debt, that is publicly sold debt, not debt we owe.

Understand, when you pay your taxes on your income, here is what we call the FICA tax, this is your payroll tax, this is the Social Security tax, this is your Medicare tax, this is the unemployment tax, this is disability.
The other part of your income tax, the corporate income tax, tariffs, excise taxes, those things are over here.

In 9 budget years, 10 years from now, 2036, almost half of nonpayroll taxes--once again, your Social Security, your Medicare, unemployment, those things--almost half of the taxes this country will collect will be just interest.

AEI did a model, Columbia, University of Minnesota, the Penn Wharton Budget Model basically built models saying, hey, when you hit this level of debt to the size of your economy, the interest you are producing makes it so you hit a death spiral.
It said in 9 budget years, in 2036, you actually have over 160 percent of debt to GDP.

That is when any damn thing, something goes wrong on the other side of the world--we have a hurricane, we have an earthquake, this and that, the credit markets, the debt markets start to get nervous, start to raise our costs.
You have such a debt and interest obligation that you have functionally no capacity.
If you don't have a 7.7 percent growth in GDP right now, you cannot keep up with how fast the debt is growing.

In 2056, that is 30 years from now, the calculations from the Treasury itself, so the Treasury is trying to sell you a 30-year bond, the Treasury itself says that we are over 250 percent of debt to GDP.
When we get down to the last couple of boards here, we are going to start to talk about what fiscal consolidation is.
Noninterest will be another 22 percent of Federal spending.
We are basically saying: Hey, we are going to have to have 35-some percent of the entire economy, 34 percent of the entire economy will just be Federal spending.
Take a look at the number of times we have done debt deals, Mr. Speaker.
I assume they are building up cash from everything, from having to pay tariff refunds to the fact that this coming January we are back up against the debt ceiling.

If we don't raise the debt ceiling, we will do what is called extraordinary measures where you basically are spending some of your cash reserves and reaching into all sorts of other accounts and spending them.
Now let's talk about the fancy term that is being thrown around: We need to do fiscal consolidation.
We have countries like, I think I actually put a couple of them on my charts, New Zealand, Canada, Australia, but there have been others that did what is called fiscal consolidation.
We are going to do some fiscal consolidation.
Every single workday I have been texting out something we call the daily debt.
Debt reduction in the United States has been and will be possible with fiscal consolidation.
That spike in spending and borrowing isn't a new bridge or new military spending.
You have to have really uncomfortable conversations, Mr. Speaker, talent-based immigration, the adoption of technology, the redesign of smart regulations, instead of bureaucratic regulations.

I have some simple suggestions: Stop the risk scoring and make it a true capitated model; get rid of the ObamaCare-type of star ratings, where you basically make it a true capitated model where you are paid to help people stay healthier.

We can make the math work, but once again, unless you are ready to deal with the reality of the math, just to cover the current growth of debt, you need a GDP that grows 7.7--not 3--7.7 percent a year.

Mr. Speaker, I wish I had the magic ability to find the powerful words to try to explain the difficulty of the finances, the reality of the math, and the threat to the Republic, but we are going to try again.
We will borrow $1 trillion every 130 days.

We are going to walk through some of the charts and some of the math, and I beg of anyone who is crazy enough to watch this, is detailed enough, is actually caring enough to watch this, I need you to open up your mind and bathe in the math with me, not the folklore.

The primary driver, if you just listen to those numbers, when interest will be $1.3 trillion this year--and I am going to show you a couple of charts--in a decade, 9 budget years, interest will be the majority of the borrowing.
We will be borrowing money to have enough cash to pay the interest.

You basically have to refinance it, so you are constantly subject to whatever the new interest rates are, and I am going to show you some charts that show much of the refinancing--because we have to refinance $10 trillion to $11 trillion this year, and a lot of that was originally borrowed at much lower interest rates.
I will tell you, today Greece can sell a 10-year bond cheaper than the United States.
The number of times I will spend 45 minutes with these slides showing what is going on, showing data that a child born today--so I have a 4-year-old we have adopted.

There are dozens and dozens and dozens of things we could be doing, but this game of sitting here and saying, well, I am going to save a million dollars here, because I am going to be speaking here for almost an hour.
During that hour we are going to borrow about $320 million.
We will often have debates here where during the time of the debate we will have borrowed substantially more than everything we debated trying to save.
God knows, I will be one of them.

In some of the reports, I think--one I got from Manhattan Institute a couple years ago--was basically saying for every dollar I will have put into Medicare I am going to get about $6, $7 back in spending.
The CBO number for 2036, 9 budget years from now--and I am going to show you the number that CBO gave us back in February is wrong because of interest rates moving up.
Hey, we are going to just do this, and then, boom, it is going to go away.
In 9 budget years, we will be at 162 percent.
I am going to give this to you in two ways.
I am going to go out and buy a 30-year bond today because I trust this place that we are going to get our fiscal act together.
I was told: David, we are going to just cover things off of the general fund accounts.
We will get people who will call us and say: David, if you just took care of waste and fraud, then we would be fine.
We will allow these taxes here to go up, but we are going to cut all this spending.
We introduced a piece of legislation over 1 year ago: MedPAC.
I am going to go down fighting for this.
If we don't get our act together, we are going to bring down the world economy with us.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRUTH ABOUT MATH
statements.title: TRUTH ABOUT MATH
sentences: In New York City, in the last 5 years the number one job creator turns out to be a Medicaid program for home visiting.
The number one job creator for half a decade in New York City is a Medicaid program.
How many of you get our daily debt?

I understand some of these numbers bounce up and down because we also had some refunding issues after the last debt ceiling issue a year ago, but in the last 12 months, we, as a government, have borrowed $2.948 trillion if you just want to do this fiscal year.
Here is the publicly sold debt, and over here is the money we borrow from the trust funds, which we do pay interest back.
Often we quote what we borrowed from the public because that is in the public bond market, but when we borrow from the trust funds--Social Security, Medicare, railroad, retirement, everything else.
Total U.S. debt as of today is $39.660 trillion.

In 6 years, when you are on Social Security and you are getting a 22 to 24 percent cut in your check, and we double poverty of seniors, 7 years from now when we double the number of baby boomers who live on the street, maybe some of this will make sense, that we should have done something much sooner, but math is math.
We are going to bring down this Republic, and it is not going to be some mob coming over the border.
I need you to understand Social Security is the number one spend.
Medicaid and the ObamaCare subsidies are the number four spend.

Mr. Speaker, if there is anyone from your staff watching--and we said we would make it public-- my team and myself were made a promise today that when we get back we are going to sit down with a couple of the committee chairs and some of my joint economic economists because we have been sitting on pieces of legislation for over a year to cut spending and borrowing, without removing services.
I will give you a simple example.

Mr. Speaker, if your staff is out there listening, I expect you and this institution to keep your promise to our team, that we are going to take these bills seriously, we are going to bring in the leadership from the committees, and we are going to pound it out how we move them forward.
By the end of this summer work period, whatever we want to call it, we are going to be at $40 trillion.
I am going to show a couple boards here.
They had numbers saying 12 to 14 years--I am going to show you that I have it even sooner on some of our data--interest is the number one expense of this government.
How many times do we get liberals saying if we just cut defense, we will balance everything?

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: OUR BORROWING IS TERRIFYING
statements.title: OUR BORROWING IS TERRIFYING
sentences: You don't pay off the debt, but you can stabilize it.
What is the number one driver of U.S. sovereign debt?

Interest this year, our model--just interest, total interest, so the interest we have to pay back the trust funds, the interest we have to pay the people who are willing to buy U.S. bonds, it is the second biggest expense in the Federal Government, so Social Security, interest, Medicare, Medicaid and ObamaCare subsidies, defense--once again, remember, defense, the thing that is in the Constitution, is actually number five.
In 9 years, what happens if a third of that money's function is just covering the interest on the debt pileup?
The rising national debt will lower wages.
Remember I was trying to talk about housing affordability?
On an average-priced home in my marketplace, which is the Phoenix, Scottsdale, Tempe sort of area, a home is just a little under $500,000 with no downpayment, so we just mortgage the whole thing.

It is a chart that makes me-- Social Security actuaries basically published a report, what, 3 weeks ago, and, yes, I have a tabbed copy, and I meant to bring it up here, but we were out doing the tour.
You tell me how the Social Security actuaries came up with this number.
Somehow the actuaries for Social Security actually say that we are going to get several years down.

When you have people talking about in 6 years to 6 years and 3 months, the Social Security actuaries have the trust fund being empty, but don't worry, because the long-run rate is we are in real trouble.
So that was my attempt to mock the Social Security actuarial report.

If the Social Security trust fund is empty in 6 years and 3 months, if the Medicare trust fund is empty pretty much at the same time, the model says that if we follow the law, those of us on Social Security will take a 22 percent to 24 percent cut.
We had dozens of things--I have been here 16 years, and I have spent most of that time trying to get this place to actually deal with the reality of let's save Social Security.
How many of us grew up always hearing you have got 23 people per retiree, and that is how we finance Social Security?
In 25 or 26 months from now, I should have double checked the math, over half of the Federal spending will go to those of us 65 and up.
Here is the Medicare and Social Security actuary's trustees saying, oh, well, we are going to go along, but magically when we get to 2030, they are going to start to go up.
The debt the United States is in is dramatically more devastating.
I am sure we are all going to get together and decide we are going to do a debt deficit commission.
That means creating a revolution of taking on the debt and deficits.
We will pay a remarkable price for the fact that the Penn Wharton models within a decade had us actually already approaching the no-go numbers of being able to sell our U.S. debt.
Mr. Speaker, I am going to take 1 or 2 seconds here to try to straighten this out just a little bit.
If you don't like math, if you don't like demographics, if you don't actually want to deal with the math I am going to give you, now would be a good time to go find something on Netflix.
So forgive me, I am going to be bouncing these around.
Now, I did this one because I am going to do a whole section here on labor force participation.
I am going to show you this chart because it is absurd.
No, I will try to go as fast as I can here.
Today, we will borrow about $7 billion.

How long is the bond market going to keep saying we are going to finance you because how much of the benefits that our brothers and sisters who are older have earned we are actually borrowing the money?
I am sure we are going to do those things to convince the bond markets that we are creditworthy because here is part of the frustration.
Tomorrow, we are going to borrow--that is like $7 billion today.
We will argue for hours here on the floor for millions.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MATH DOESN'T LIE
statements.title: MATH DOESN'T LIE
sentences: Mr. Speaker, this is going to be another presentation of basically budget, debt, my frustration with this place, and my frustration with telling the truth.

This government has made a decision we will need 104 percent of that little boy's lifetime earnings just to pay the Federal Government pensions, to cover Social Security, Medicare, military retirement, our retirement, 104 percent of the generation of young people today, we are so upside-down mathematically.

However, not once did someone come behind these microphones and say that one of the primary problems in affordability of you being able to purchase a home, Mr. Speaker, is the fact that if we had a normal debt load, then you would be paying 5.5 percent on today's 30-year loan.
We will exist in a fear of the weekly and monthly debt auctions.

We are paying 1 point higher because of the scale of U.S. sovereign debt borrowing that when you buy that 30-year mortgage, Mr. Speaker, on an average priced home--and I think we used an average priced home in Arizona, not here in D.C.--you are going to pay about $2,500 more, and over the life of that loan, $76,000 more.
Do you want us to tell you things that set off a good dopamine hit, that make you feel this, but don't tell you the truth about the demographics, debt, and deficit?
If you do the last 12 months--understand there is a blip in there because we had the extraordinary measures where we didn't have a debt ceiling and we had to refund it.
Remember, Mr. Speaker--I am going to try to make this point a couple of times through the presentation in some of the last slides--the primary driver of the debt is not a tax cut over here.
We would actually have to have an honest conversation of some of the fraud we found in things like Medicaid and Medicare.
You don't have to score it as more long-term debt.

That means, in 9 budget years, 31 percent of every tax dollar that is paid, meaning income tax, payroll tax, and tariffs, everything coming in, in 9 budget years, 31 percent of all those tax collections will be just interest.
Remember, Medicare and Social Security are pay-as-you-go programs.
I did the presentation a couple weeks ago on the Social Security actuary report.
If we followed the law--I think the Social Security actuary report is wrong on their math, but they said in 6 years, 3 months, you get a 22 percent cut.
Yay, we are going to double the number of homelessness living on the street of baby boomers.
Workers per Social Security beneficiary.

That is why every month when Social Security checks go out the door, the Social Security administrator reaches over to their special Treasury bills and say, Treasury, we are short because the payroll taxes don't cover all the checks going out the door.
In about 25, maybe 26 months, over half of the Federal Government spending will go to those 65 and up.
I am a believer we have to have a revolution in how we provide government services: the adoption of technology, the elimination of excess positions, those things.
All that has passed so far is about $7 billion in actual spending cuts that have made it through Congress, Senate, and to the President's desk for his signature.
We will have moved into our earned benefit years: Medicare, Social Security, military or public service retirement, whatever it is.
I will argue this debt, unless we find a way to start stabilizing it, we are not going to make it another 250 years.
So we are going to walk behind these mikes over and over and over and desperately try to find whatever the dopamine hit is of the day, and yet, we will borrow another $6 billion, $7 billion today.
I also tried--and I am going to do it again because apparently I didn't do it very well.
It is going to be a conversation of how we are going to fix it.
I am going to produce a whole bunch of boards here.
My rule used to be that I am going to give you the problem, Mr. Speaker, and then I am going to give you a series of solutions.
We are not allowed to talk about that in an election year, but we will fix it next year.
Mr. Speaker, I am going to show you some charts here that in 9 years how big that math actually gets.
What has made it through the legislative process is about $7 billion, basically what we will borrow today.
Of course, we are going to work on that and talk about it next year.
If you don't see the math problem--I am going to bite my tongue.
CBO last February said, hey, we are going to be borrowing $3.1 trillion that year, 2.1 of it will be just interest.
In 9 years, we will have 70 million, so we will actually have fewer people under 18, and we will have 76 million, 65 and up.
Just send us a couple thousand dollars, and we will send you a DOGE check.

Then you take other calculations that I am not going to geek out too much on: labor force participation, the number of our population that is actually in the labor force, and then we have a math problem.
With that, Mr. Speaker, I will go back and look at all of the angry comments I am going to get because, once again, telling the truth means you get the crap kicked out of you around here.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PRESENTING THE MATH
statements.title: PRESENTING THE MATH
sentences: One, we are going to actually talk about the real driver of interest rates, housing affordability.
Yesterday, in my Joint Economic Committee, we did a high-level fraud in government- sponsored healthcare, Medicaid, and other programs--some wonderful data.
Why this is so important is that I keep trying to explain to people to understand that Social Security is the number one spend.
Medicaid and ObamaCare, ACA subsidies, are about a trillion.

If anyone was paying attention in the math there, if we are going to take in $5, $5.5, $5.25 trillion in tax receipts, did you notice that by the time I got to the Medicaid ACA subsidies, we were out of money?
Housing affordability sensitivity to interest rates--think about this.

Did you hear a single discussion around this place saying, hey, we are going to talk about housing affordability, maybe we could actually convince the debt markets we are going to stabilize our borrowing.

Look, when you have an almost $40 trillion debt, CBO's own report said in 9 budget years--and this is without the recent higher interest rates, without some of the additional supplementals and other borrowing and spending we are about to do--in 9 years, the deficit is going to be $3.1 trillion, and $2.1 trillion of that was just interest. $1 trillion was actually the structural deficit.
This isn't something where foreign nationals sneak into the country and set up a scam.
So you can have your child, your cousin, your sister visit you on your Medicaid.
Now you start to see what I mean when I talk about that the debt is substantially demographics.
Let's see how many more of these we want to torture you with.
But debt held by the public per capita--and remember when we were in 2011, we were basically $33,000 per capita.
Just trying to make the argument, Medicare, Social Security, today's worker pays for todays' retiree.
That trust fund in the Social Security actuary report that came out a week ago basically says that in a little over 6 years, it is gone.

Now, we can geek out for a while and explain that we already started borrowing that money internally because Treasury has already spent it, but Social Security holds those T bills so they cash them in.
But under current law, when that trust fund is gone in 6 years, 3 months, everyone over 65 getting a Social Security check under current law gets a 22 to 24 percent cut.
U.S. debt is raising the cost for all of you.
I am going to try three different things in this presentation.

Then, the third thing, we are going to step on one of the third rails of politics, and we are going to tell the truth about demographics and the financing of Medicare and some of the things we are going to have to do to actually keep it stable.
That means this year, my math is we are going to borrow about $2 to $2.3 trillion.
One of the hardest parts is having an honest conversation around here--I am going to show you.
What is the likelihood that we are going to convince our brothers and sisters here that we are going to borrow less money?
The frustrating thing is you and I will go home, and we will have a townhall or meetings, and this and that, and the public will turn to us and say: It is all waste and fraud.
I am going to show you the slides.
We are going to bounce back and forth to try to make the point that it is how we have designed the policy.
We will basically go from $1 trillion last year to $2 trillion per year.

What are we about to do to grow productivity so fast that we can make up for a country that is now at zero population growth and that Census had a prediction that sometime in the next 5 years, we will actually have 1 or 2 years with negative population growth.
We will double the poverty of seniors at that time.
I will give you the classic example of 15 years ago, Hepatitis C, we had hospitals all around the country getting ready to put up liver transplant centers.
I am going to see if I have one last board here.
Is this really what we decided we are going to do to our kids and our grandkids?

Take a look at the Social Security actuary report of the suppression of working people's wages because of the importation of low-skill populations.
Pay someone and then let's hire lots of auditors, lots of lawyers, lots of law enforcement, and let's chase it down.
Now, we need to actually add some of the definitions and the mechanics of how we are going to take it on.
I will argue that the model we use today is perverse.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: EFFECT OF WASTE AND FRAUD
statements.title: EFFECT OF WASTE AND FRAUD
sentences: Today was also the issuance of the annual Social Security actuarial report.
If you have a Social Security number being used over and over and over, maybe there is a problem.
It is like the absurdity of--absolutely, we all vote for it--let's do a balanced budget.
We have to cut almost half of all Federal spending because of the economic effects.

Our economists think we can nail down a third of this waste and fraud if you just take some of the legislation we have worked on for years of the use of data, matching benefits, matching Social Security numbers, matching addresses, matching codes coming out of CMS, matching these things.
An MRI scan, an ultrasound, a CT, an x-ray.

Now, the number of times I have come behind this microphone and said Social Security trust fund, the Medicare trust fund, a little over 6 years, and I have actually had debates--as a matter of fact, we had some sparring today--where I spoke for a couple moments, and the Democrat who was speaking said: Yes, but illegals pay into Social Security.

Yes, but if you actually read the Social Security actuary report, it would have shown you, yes, they are paying into fake Social Security numbers--okay, that is a little money--but the suppression of wages that happen from the millions and millions and millions and millions of people that came across the border in the Biden years is greater than.
I know, it would require reading the Social Security actuary report and maybe pulling out a calculator and doing some math.
They are out hanging drywall, and now they are competing with how many potentially millions of people that came across the border during those years that are competing with them selling their labor.

The fastest way you get affordability is wage growth because to magically start to make prices come down, you have to change systems and supply chains, legalize automation of ports, all the things that the unions and everyone else is going to come lobby and scream at us.
Let's actually walk through a couple things that were out there in that Social Security actuary report today and from last year so there is an understanding.
The only controversy right now is the Social Security actuary report that came out today said it is a 22 percent cut in 6 years.

Instead, in this place--and God knows I have gone through it election after election after election--where the Democrat consultants say: Oh, Schweikert used the words ``Social Security,'' he used the word ``Medicare,'' let's beat the crap out of him.

I have done presentation after presentation after presentation showing just even raising the cap doesn't come close to covering, 2033, Mr. Speaker, the money needed to cover the Social Security shortfall and the Medicare shortfall--because, remember, the Medicare trust fund is also empty at the same time.
Let's take a look, just to understand how fast the Social Security trust fund is eroding.
Every month, Social Security says that we hold all these, let's call them magic Social Security T bills.
They call the Treasury and say: Hey, guys, I have to make my monthly Social Security checks.
This month, they don't have enough, so they sell some debt.
Social Security, Medicare, and net interest account for 81 percent of the spending growth over the next 10 years.
CBO calculated that in 2036, the annual debt will be $3.1 trillion, $2.1 trillion of it just being interest and the $1 trillion being the baseline deficit.
Once we cover Social Security, once we cover Medicare, then we have to pay the interest bill.
In 2026, old-age and survivors account with Social Security, annual balances are much worse than previously predicted.
They are actually much worse than the numbers the Social Security actuaries are using.

The head of Social Security is going to be in front of Ways and Means in the next couple of weeks, and we need to ask him why the other demographers are actually saying that fertility calculations in future years are much worse than Social Security is using.

We need to come up with a way to either say that when we produce the Social Security actuary report, we as policymakers should actually be reading it and doing something instead of hiding from it, and maybe also add in there saying we are going to also other academic demographers, and we are also going to add maybe the Census Bureau, which has had, historically, the most accurate numbers of fertility rates.
Please, Social Security actuaries, I look forward to the explanation of how you came up with that because no one else has that number.
The national effects of Social Security insolvency is basically the depletion of the trust fund in what, 6 years, 3 months on recipients, 24, 27 percent benefit cuts over those years.
The Social Security actuary report said 22.
Monthly cuts exceed $500, so in 29 States, basically they are adding up how much of the population's average income they paid into Social Security.
Remember, a number of people don't understand, Mr. Speaker, Social Security is means-adjusted.
High-income earners get less back of the taxes they paid in.
Insolvency of Social Security, what does it mean to my recipients, my folks who receive a Social Security check in Arizona?

Yet, the political class, because they either are good at math or they are terrified to tell the voters the truth, on Social Security, you functionally get, for the average couple, the money you put in plus a tiny bit.

If 25 years ago we had done what President Bush and others had talked about saying--just a little bit of your Social Security money going into side accounts--the retiring population today would be so much more prosperous.
Democrats and unions crushed that.
The hardest part is also showing chart after chart after chart--it is Medicare that is actually the biggest contributor to U.S. sovereign debt.

What would that be worth if we just fixed the misalignment in Medicare Advantage, let alone all the durable medical equipment and all the things that are now happening with Medicaid, whether it be the scams we found in New York, where you hire family members to be the visitor.
Mr. Speaker, I am fixated on debt, deficits, and demographics because I am going to argue that we have a country that about every 13\1/2\ seconds we are borrowing a million dollars.
I promise you I will read it over the next couple of weeks.
I am going to make some commentary.
Look, it is huge, but I am going to show you some of the charts of what the reality is on the percentage of our spending.
From joint economists, our best estimate right now is we are going to borrow $2 trillion this year.
My personal number--I am the outlier--is we are going to borrow about $2.2 trillion, but then I am a little more pessimistic.
We are going to credit that back because we are not writing them off.
This is using the most optimistic number saying, Mr. Speaker, we are going to be able to stomp out every bit of fraud, waste, misalignment, and exploitation in this government.
We are going to spend--estimated government fraud is almost 7.8 percent of the outlays for this year.
Do you really think we are going to get all of it?
I will tell you, some of the lobbyists marching down the hallways hate this stuff.

Understand, when you get the politician in front of you saying: We are going to stomp out waste and fraud, and then they make it sound like it is someone from the other side of the world stealing from us, that is some of it.
We will double the number of baby boomers who live on the street 7 years from now.
Then you will get some idiot who says: Well, we will just raise the taxes, that covers it.
Now, we are going to pay the price for it.
You start to look at some of these, Mr. Speaker, and the reason I put this one up, and I will tell you, this is done by my economists and some of the others.

Now, I would argue it is caused by a number of social policies and then other things that the Democrats promoted, but now some of us have to figure out a way to manage this and tell the truth on how we are going to keep our promises to seniors.
These gaps, because they are calculating, suddenly we are going to actually have fertility rates going up.
We are going to create a wave of poverty, but, hey, we are just going to tax the hell out of people who are still working.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEBT CLOCK TICKING
statements.title: DEBT CLOCK TICKING
sentences: I also need to actually try to explain debt and deficits when our borrowing is stunning.
So we have a con artist that set up an internet company, got a government contract.
Maybe that is the reason we don't touch it enough because the fraud is in Medicare, the fraud is in Medicaid, and the fraud is in other programs that are on autopilot.

You get this benefit, except within there, particularly in the Medicaid system--you have seen the analysis the Joint Economic Committee has done, or my joint economic Republicans have done over the last year on the number of ways States--States--are the driver of the fraud.

If I came to you right now and told you that New York, the number of home healthcare aides--this is a Medicaid program where grandma is poor, she needs help, I have someone at home who needs help, and there is a program that came really out of COVID or was expanded out of COVID where I can actually hire my friends, my families, my nieces, my nephews.

Remember, if New York had the same cost of its Medicaid system--not Medicare--Medicaid--this is healthcare for the poor--and they had the same average cost as the rest of the country, it is $50 billion a year.
They must have some magic with their Medicaid system because they are able to create their own codes.

This is an example, when you hear the politicians say ``I am going to get rid of waste and fraud,'' and we make it sound like it is somebody snuck across the border and stole money or someone on the internet from the other side of the world stole money, all of those are true, but it is the design of the system that we have developed.

In the end of this stack, I am going to walk through a series of solutions, but understand that when we tried to just trim down some of the growth of Medicaid spending last summer and the left just attacked, attacked, attacked, and we would show, but what about this fraud, what about this fraud, what about this fraud, the discussion goes silent.
All right. ``Top 15 Producers by Medicaid Spending.'' Personal care services.

If we are going to actually try to convince the brothers and sisters, the taxpayers, the voters, and the American citizenry of what is going on--debt and deficits and demographics in this State--that in a little over 6 years, Medicare trust fund is empty, and hospitals, those that get their Medicare part A money, are going to take a 12 percent cut, and guess what is also happening around this same time.
The Social Security trust fund is empty, and people on Social Security, under the current law, are going to take a 24 percent cut, and we are going to double poverty.
If scammers are bleeding our Medicaid systems around the State, why is it so hard to actually say-- we hold hearings on this.

You start to look at some of these things: unemployment fraud, $32.6 billion; Medicaid fraud, that one was only $178 million; homeless spending, let's see, billions and billions, doesn't actually give me a number.

There is the fraud where somebody stole your Social Security number and did this, but the real money is how poorly we designed the programs that are meant to help our brothers and sisters, particularly those in poverty.

We have been now working on this for months and months and months. ``Sham hospice schemes are bilking Medicare,'' and some Medicaid, ``and harming California seniors.'' We actually believe this scheme--if you have been reading the papers, L.A. Times and I believe The Wall Street Journal have done stories on this.
Medicare Advantage is now 55 percent of all of our seniors who choose Medicare.

How does someone not catch it when the same Social Security number is used over and over, when there is no Social Security number, when the same location has more people signed up for a benefit than there are people in that immediate area?
Many of them had been buying your personal ID, your personal information, on the dark web, signing you up, putting you in debt.

All right, a little bit more, and this one, I happen to actually have had a fascinating experience with: ``Arizona sober living crisis: 140 indicted in billion-dollar Medicaid scheme.'' We think it is $2.8 billion.
It turns out, they were being driven down to Phoenix, being stuck in a sober living home, being billed to the Medicaid system, which we call AHCCCS, Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System.
The Justice Department has cracked down on a Pakistani national who allegedly orchestrated a $650 million fraud scheme in Arizona's Medicaid system.
Attach it to your smartphone, and it travels with you.
The Social Security numbers don't match.
And then we will hire some law enforcement.

The reality of the waste and fraud is huge, but the scale of our borrowing, the scale of our debt, which is driven by our demographics-- next year, we are going to have fewer under 18 than we had 20 years ago and double the number of 65 and up.
In 28 months, over half of Federal spending will go to our brothers and sisters who are 65 and up.
We stopped the way we have screwed up the model on Medicare, Medicaid, and so many of the programs which were designed to help people and not enrich fraudsters.
Mr. Speaker, we are going to actually try to do something that is a little complex, so I apologize.
If I start speaking like a machine gun--once again, I have had a stunning amount of coffee--just wave at me, and I will slow down.
I am going to try to actually explain and walk through what we talk about constantly, and that is waste and fraud.
I have got three silos here, and I am going to try to fight for some understanding: What is real in its fiscal impact.
It is something simple, but I am going to use it as a benchmark.
I need to put this in perspective, because so often here we get our brothers and sisters, Members of Congress, come behind these microphones, and we talk about what we are going to save on something.
I am going to do this three or four times.
We are going to borrow about $7 billion today, so $50 billion starts making an impact.

Does this meet your definition of waste and fraud, because HHS--we are going to walk through a series of things that MedPAC has tried to identify for years that we can't seem to get enough votes here to even run a piece of legislation to try to fix it.
I am going to show you a couple where there are t's in front of it, trillions in front of it.
I am going to actually show you--let's just talk about it before I try to show you.
I introduced a piece of legislation a year ago to not cut services but to get rid of the risk scoring and the star rating, all the ways it was being defrauded, and that is what this board is about.

That is actually, if you want to start to stabilize, even demonstrate to bond markets we are starting to take serious our leakage, our bleeding, our borrowing--remember, we are going to borrow $7 billion to $8 billion just today.
Keep that in mind because I am going to walk you through some of the solutions, but this stuff is absolutely outrageous, and then you start to take a look.
Then, our model is, we are going to indict a bunch of people.
Now, all the money got shipped overseas, so we are not going to get any of it back, but we are going to file indictments on people who are not in the country anymore or were never in the country.
We are going to allow this handful of companies to do it because at least they have some trusted history, and they were screaming at us.
Look, I am going to do a little skipping to the end because we are running out of time.
Here are our payees, the people we are going to pay checks to, we owe, because as the county treasurer you are the guy issuing the checks to pay for things.
How many of you would build a business model where I am going to pay 6 percent, 7 percent of my payments are going to be fraud, but don't worry about that.
Eventually we are going to hire a bunch of auditors.
Then we will hire some lawyers.
And then we will try to go recover the money.
And most of the time we never get to put someone in prison, but we will get to do great press releases.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: UNSUSTAINABLE DEBT
statements.title: UNSUSTAINABLE DEBT
sentences: This time, I am just going to try to be the guy who cares about financing the U.S. debt and what the hell is going on right now.

There were no ideas with it, there was no discipline with it, there was no telling the truth with it, but we did a resolution so we can all put it on our political brochures and say we voted for a balanced budget.
I have got to cut half of U.S. Federal spending.

Now, that will balance out a little bit because there is a spike in there from last year's debt ceiling when we had to refund many of the accounts, but when you look at this chart, there is something really important to get your heads around.
Social Security, $1.6 trillion; interest, 1.2; Medicare, about 1.1.
Number four is actually Medicaid and ObamaCare subsidies.
However, down the hallway and in the basement, a Republican Study Committee was trying to do a debt fraud forum.

Are we a society where the desire for government spending--because there are tens of thousands of people from home, from lobbyists, others walking up and down our hallways, in our offices all day long telling us how much they care about the debt and deficits, and then they demand more money.
The entire world--at least most of the industrialized world--is bingeing on debt.
You have to understand: We have to convince the world debt markets that we are going to tame inflation, that we are creditworthy, and that we are going to get our act together.

There is a report that came out just about an hour ago--honestly, I have only read the first half of it--that basically was doing the calculations that even publicly sold debt, in 9 budget years, will be over 126 percent of debt-to-GDP.
In slightly over 6 years, if you are on Social Security, you get a 24-percent cut in your check.
In a little over 6 years, the Social Security trust fund is empty.
You will have some of your own people in a primary saying: He talked about Social Security and Medicare.

For the idiots that go around saying, ``Well, we will just raise this tax,'' understand that, in 2033, to cover the shortfall of the Medicare and Social Security trust funds is over $638 billion just that year, just to cover the first year, and then it goes up and goes up and goes up.
You figure out and tell me how I am going to finance Social Security and Medicare.
You tell me how I finance the debt.
All we focused on was what was going on in Medicare, not Medicaid, the benefit we promised our seniors.
You have an MRI, an x-ray, an ultrasound, and a CT.
In 28, 29 months, over half of our Federal spending will go to our brothers and sisters who are 65 and up, and I will be one of them.
Debt financing costs double in 10 years.
The CBO baseline budget from last February had, in 9 budget years, the U.S. debt--now, this is before the move in interest rates.
In 9 years, U.S. debt, borrowing, will be $3.1 trillion.
That is $2.1 trillion of that borrowing in 9 budget years, 10 years from now, is just interest. $1 trillion is the structural debt.
We are supposed to tell stories about crazy things, or bad people, or illegal immigrants.
We say that over 10 years that is over $2 trillion on today's projected budget and spending and current debt.

I am going to do this three or four times in this presentation, so if anyone is listening, think about this: From February until this week, the movement on U.S. interest rates, if you do it over 10 years, it is over $2 trillion of additional interest.

As I am traveling around the State, I will do part of my presentation on what is really happening in the Federal Government and why it is so important to get the finances of your own State really solid because some of the revenue sharing that goes to the States--which is almost half my State's budget, our total spending--is going to start to dry up because every dime we send to the States is borrowed.

Here is the problem in this place: Because of the financial illiteracy--sorry, I withdraw that, that is being a little mean--the lack of batteries in the calculators around here, you will see Members come behind these microphones on both sides: We are going to save $1 million, $10 million, $20 million on this, and we will have borrowed more money on the debate on the piece of legislation than the bill saves.
We will borrow over $7.7-plus billion today.
Those people go, yay, we are going to get smaller.
You tell me how I am going to convince the bond markets not to keep raising our interest rates.
We are going to run more fake ``we are going to balance the budget'' bills with no plans.

Social Security, Medicare, and net interest account for 80 percent of the spending growth over the next nine budget years.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: THE MATH
statements.title: THE MATH
sentences: One of these days we are going to have not enough noise about the facts, the numbers, the data, the debt, those things that we can come in and sort of do our boards, our charts, on things that actually reduce spending and modernize.
Mr. Speaker, I have come behind the microphone many times and talked about the scale of debt.
If you are a country that needs to borrow about $6 billion a day, we borrow about $6 billion a day, what happens in a world where you actually--the liquidity of the debt markets.

When you have a country that has $900 billion, maybe a trillion dollars of U.S. sovereign debt, and you walk in the door and say: We want to renegotiate some of our trade pact with you or we want to build an actual trade pact with you, they look at you and say: But we right now take those dollars that you send us because you have been buying our stuff, and we are buying your debt.

The fact of the matter is if you are a country that is borrowing $6 billion a day, does anyone understand the fragility, and I am going use that fancy word a couple of times, because also interest--we are actually seeing some indications that when we get out of extraordinary measures--for everyone who doesn't understand, we hit the debt ceiling a couple months ago.
We worked on the dataset saying: When we finally raise the debt ceiling, let's say a month or two from now, Treasury is going to need to pay back those dollars plus the interest.

Just be prepared for what is really going on in the interest rate markets, the debt markets, and will we be beyond some of the discussions of trade where countries like Japan aren't leaking stories that they are going to use our debt as leverage against us.
The chart here and the bar here I want people to pay attention to is Moody's, who has this whole thing where they do analytics on debt and spending.

Mr. Speaker, their estimate is in 9 years, 30 percent of U.S. tax collections, that is everything, corporate, individual, estate, the tariffs, everything, they estimate in 9 years, 30 percent of all those tax receipts that come into the Federal Government will just pay interest.

I showed some charts a couple weeks ago that showed an estimate that if U.S. debt went up 1 percent in interest--selling our bonds, if interest rates went up 1 percent on us, in that 9 budget years, it is not 30 percent of tax receipts that go to just interest, it is 45 percent.
Remember, when we finish this fiscal year, the CBO estimate is U.S. sovereign debt, all of it, the gross debt, will be at $37.2 trillion.

The thing we are not supposed to tell people because it hurts their feelings, gets them upset, but it is called math, is over the next 10 years, the vast majority of debt is interest and healthcare costs, mostly Medicare.
Unless you are willing to have honest conversations about debt deficits and demographics, the demographics is the driver of U.S. sovereign debt.
The thing about this, the ACA, many of you know it as ObamaCare, it is a financing bill.
Medicare for All is a financing bill.

When you run around thinking that the United States is the gold standard, we are also screwing up our extraordinary privilege of having the world reserve currency, and the dollar is coming back to us because you start to see some slowdown in buying U.S. sovereign debt.
We are not coming to market with new debt.
I think I have a chart that shows that the United States will consume 30 to 40 percent of all of the world capital that is going to sovereign debt in the next decade.
When we borrow money from the Social Security trust fund or these other things, which all that money has already been borrowed, we have to pay interest back.

When Social Security redeems its bonds, we pay them back the money they need for that next month's checks to come out because, remember, Social Security is running about a little less than a structural 25 percent shortfall from tax collections to checks out the door.
Starting at about 2022, our interest became more than the Department of Defense budget.
Social Security comes in at about $1.480 trillion.
Defense right now is actually coming in around No. 4--Social Security, interest, Medicare, defense.
If you tell the truth about the drivers of U.S. sovereign debt, you will never end up on MSNBC or FOX News or any of those because no one wants to hear the actual math.

Yet, if we were to do the Senate's reconciliation budget, which has almost no cuts in spending in it, we will borrow approximately--I am conflating publicly sold debt with the debt we would create in the next 10 years.

Does this body, the lobbyists in the hallways, the groups in the hallways demanding more spending, or any of the staffers who might not have a life so they are watching this really think that the bond markets aren't going to go: They are doubling U.S. debt, maybe we should ask for a little premium, which is called term premium, on U.S. sovereign debt, but I just showed you and told you what happens if we go up 1 percent.

Just as in the article, we are already up against the leverage of Japan in this one, but I don't know why it is not about other countries using the fact that we have used them and we have needed them to finance our debt.
If that becomes the perception in the world debt markets, we are going to pay a penalty for it, and that penalty is really expensive.

We have been working on that to sort of modernize it, and so for all the lobbyists who are making money trying to beat us up for trying to actually fix it, I will warn you that the legislation is almost done.
We are going to do what about it?

We are going to squeeze out our ability to do the things that we believe are important for protecting the Constitution and the society because, God forbid--the bond markets forbid--that we all of a sudden start to have a spike in interest rates.
Paygo, how many times--paygo, I actually think was a Democratic proposal from years ago that, if we are going to add new spending beyond the 5-year window, there needs to be an offset.
We tell people that we are going to be fiscally disciplined.
As soon as it is uncomfortable, then we will just waive it.
We are going to spend over $68 trillion in the next 10 years.
What took us 240 years to build, we will double in 10 years, or come close to doubling in 10 years.
We are going to pay you back appropriately.
Then we intend to leverage them?
Mr. Speaker, I am going to go back to the office and have more coffee.

statements.title: ECONOMIC ANXIETY
sentences: I am going to actually walk through some debt and deficit numbers, interest, those things that are scaring my economists, myself half to death; and then I am going to touch on some of the--and it is a technical economics term--bedwetting in regard to the reconciliation budget and how people are making things up.
